_status: From the medical lead's workbook (Scientific References sheet). Do not edit by hand: re-run backend/scripts/import_medical.py. A reference without a URL keeps the sheet's note, or "needs verification" when the sheet has none.

references.authors: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer (OCHMO)
references.title: NASA Spaceflight Human-System Standard Volume 1, Revision C: Crew Health (NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1)
references.findings: Establishes Agency-level human health and medical care technical standards to optimize crew health and fitness across all mission phases.
references.values: Defines permissible exposure limits, physiological monitoring standards, medical care levels, and ALARA radiation exposure criteria [V1 4029].

references.authors: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer (OCHMO)
references.title: NASA Spaceflight Human-System Standard Volume 2, Revision F: Human Factors, Habitability, and Environmental Health
references.findings: Establishes engineering and environmental requirements for spacecraft habitability, life support, and crew interface design.
references.values: [V2 6004] requires one-hour average habitable-volume ppCO2 <=3 mmHg. Off-nominal actions are mission-specific.
references.verification: Updated to currently active revision; detailed sections require source audit

references.title: Human Cardiorespiratory and Orthostatic Intolerance Evidence Book
references.findings: Documents microgravity-induced cephalad fluid shifts, stroke volume reductions, baroreflex resetting, and post-flight orthostatic intolerance mechanisms.
references.values: Post-flight stand test tachycardia (HR > 120 bpm) and orthostatic systolic blood pressure drops > 25 mmHg observed in ~65% of long-duration astronauts.
references.verification: Needs citation/claim verification (missing direct source URL)

references.authors: Stahn, A. C., Werner, A., Opatz, O., et al.
references.title: Increased core body temperature in astronauts during long-duration space missions
references.findings: Identifies persistent core temperature elevation in microgravity ('space fever') resulting from altered thermoregulation and convective heat dissipation.
references.values: Resting core temperature increases by 1.0°C over 2.5 months on ISS, with delayed heat dissipation during physical exercise (>39.5°C).
references.verification: Needs citation/claim verification (missing direct source URL)

references.authors: Barger, L. K., Flynn-Evans, E. E., Kubey, A., et al.
references.title: Prevalence of sleep deficiency and hypnotic use among astronauts before, during, and after spaceflight
references.findings: Demonstrates pervasive sleep deficiency in spaceflight, documented by wrist actigraphy and sleep logs, with pervasive circadian desynchrony.
references.values: In-flight sleep duration averaged < 6.0 hours per night; 75% of crew reported hypnotic medication usage during missions.
references.verification: Needs citation/claim verification (missing direct source URL)

references.authors: Basner, M., Dinges, D. F., Mollicone, D., et al.
references.title: Cognitive performance in long-duration spaceflight and associations with environmental factors
references.findings: Evaluates neurobehavioral performance on the Cognition test battery and PVT, linking operational fatigue and elevated cabin CO2 to cognitive lapses.
references.values: PVT lapses increase significantly when sleep duration is <6h or cabin ppCO2 exceeds 2.0 mmHg; executive function shows speed-accuracy tradeoffs.
references.verification: Needs citation/claim verification (missing direct source URL)

references.authors: Lang, T., LeBlanc, A., Evans, H., et al.
references.title: Cortical and trabecular bone mineral loss from the spine and hip in long-duration spaceflight
references.findings: Quantifies monthly bone mineral density decline and structural decay in weight-bearing bones due to skeletal mechanical unloading in microgravity.
references.values: Trabecular bone loss averaged 1.0% to 1.5% per month in calcaneus, femoral neck, and spine; serum CTX elevated >50% above pre-flight baseline.
references.verification: Bibliography corrected; verify any CTX threshold separately

references.authors: Crucian, B. E., Choukèr, A., Simpson, R. J., et al.
references.title: Immune system dysregulation during spaceflight: Potential countermeasures for deep space missions
references.findings: Reviews comprehensive immunological alterations in astronauts, including peripheral blood leukopenia, cytokine shifts, and latent herpesvirus shedding.
references.values: Pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha) elevated >30-50% during long-duration flight; EBV and VZV viral shedding detected in >50% of crew.

references.authors: National Council on Radiation Protection and Measurements (NCRP)
references.title: NCRP Report No. 153: Information Needed to Make Radiation Protection Recommendations for Space Missions Beyond LEO
references.findings: Establishes radiation biodosimetry guidelines, organ dose equivalents, and acute exposure thresholds for deep space and planetary exploration.
references.values: Short-term 30-day limit of 250 mGy-Eq for blood-forming organs; career effective dose limit 600 mSv; alert threshold for SPE flux > 10 mSv/hr.
references.verification: Bibliographic year corrected; exposure limits must be checked against current NASA rules

references.title: Adult Basic Life Support: 2025 Guidelines
references.findings: Assessment of unresponsive patients, emergency response, high-quality CPR, AED use
references.values: CPR 100-120/min; 5-6cm; pulse check <=10sec for healthcare provider
references.verification: Verified guideline; applicability to spaceflight requires mission review

references.authors: American Heart Association / American Red Cross
references.title: 2024 First Aid Guidelines
references.findings: Prompt emergency assessment for acute chest pain; recognize limitations of first aid and oximetry

references.title: When to Call 911 About High Blood Pressure
references.findings: Extreme BP requires context of symptoms and repeated measurement
references.values: >180/120 with concerning symptoms warrants urgent emergency response

references.title: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026: Glycemic Goals and Hypoglycemia
references.values: <70; <54 mg/dL; severe impairment regardless of value

references.title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2 Revision F
references.findings: Nominal spacecraft CO2 level is a one-hour average requirement
references.verification: Verified active revision; off-nominal thresholds require mission rules

references.title: Evaluation of a Novel Basic Life Support Method in Simulated Microgravity
references.findings: ER CPR method supported in short simulated microgravity test
references.values: Not a clinical certification; short test (3 min)

references.title: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation during spaceflight: a guideline for CPR in microgravity
references.findings: Recommends ER as initial BLS; transition to restrained patient/ALS method
references.values: Method depends on training and mission resources

references.title: Pulse Oximeters
references.findings: Accuracy limitations from motion, skin temperature, perfusion, pigmentation
